bugs.name: Entamoeba histolytica
bugs.symptoms: Bloody diarrhea; RUQ pain with 'anchovy paste' liver abscess

bugs.name: Giardia lamblia
bugs.symptoms: Foul-smelling, fatty, non-bloody diarrhea and bloating

bugs.name: Trichomonas vaginalis
bugs.symptoms: Frothy green-yellow discharge; strawberry cervix; motile trophozoite

bugs.name: Trypanosoma brucei gambiense
bugs.symptoms: Chronic course; Winterbottom's sign; somnolence progressing to coma
bugs.treatment: Fexinidazole (oral); NECT for severe CNS disease

bugs.name: Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense
bugs.symptoms: Acute, rapidly fatal; fever, lymphadenopathy, CNS decline
bugs.treatment: Fexinidazole early; melarsoprol + prednisolone for late CNS

bugs.name: Trypanosoma cruzi
bugs.symptoms: Romaña sign acutely; dilated cardiomyopathy, megaesophagus, megacolon

bugs.name: Leishmania donovani
bugs.symptoms: Fever, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia; fatal if untreated

bugs.name: Leishmania braziliensis
bugs.symptoms: Disfiguring nasal and oropharyngeal mucosal destruction
bugs.treatment: Liposomal amphotericin B or pentavalent antimonials

bugs.name: Toxoplasma gondii
bugs.symptoms: Ring-enhancing brain lesions in AIDS; congenital chorioretinitis-hydrocephalus-calcifications

bugs.name: Staphylococcus aureus
bugs.symptoms: Furuncle/carbuncle; pus-producing wound; coagulase-positive

bugs.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
bugs.symptoms: Indolent device infection; biofilm-forming, coagulase-negative

bugs.name: Staphylococcus saprophyticus
bugs.symptoms: Dysuria, frequency; coagulase-negative, novobiocin-resistant

bugs.name: Streptococcus pyogenes
bugs.symptoms: Bright raised erysipelas; pharyngitis; pain out of proportion in nec fasc
bugs.treatment: Penicillin; surgical debridement for necrotizing fasciitis

bugs.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
bugs.symptoms: Necrotic ulcer with black eschar in neutropenia; blue-green pigment

bugs.name: Cutibacterium acnes
bugs.symptoms: Inflammatory comedones; gram-positive aerotolerant rod

bugs.name: Actinomyces israelii
bugs.symptoms: Lumpy jaw with draining sinus tracts; yellow sulfur granules

bugs.name: Mycobacterium ulcerans
bugs.symptoms: Painless slowly enlarging skin ulcer with undermined edges

bugs.name: Parvovirus B19
bugs.symptoms: Slapped-cheek rash, lacy reticular trunk rash; aplastic crisis, hydrops fetalis
bugs.treatment: Supportive; IVIG or intrauterine transfusion in at-risk groups

bugs.name: Yersinia pestis
bugs.symptoms: Painful inguinal buboes; flea bite; digital gangrene

bugs.name: Yersinia enterocolitica
bugs.symptoms: RLQ pain mimicking appendicitis with bloody diarrhea in a child
bugs.treatment: Often self-limited; severe cases doxycycline or TMP-SMX

bugs.name: Bacillus anthracis
bugs.symptoms: Painless black eschar with edema; mediastinal widening in inhalation form
bugs.treatment: Ciprofloxacin or doxycycline plus additional agents

bugs.name: Borrelia burgdorferi
bugs.symptoms: Erythema migrans bull's-eye rash; AV block, Bell's palsy, Lyme arthritis

bugs.name: Borrelia recurrentis
bugs.geography: Refugee camps, war zones (Ethiopia, Sudan, Somalia)
bugs.symptoms: Recurrent febrile episodes from antigenic variation

bugs.name: Leptospira interrogans
bugs.geography: Tropical regions; Hawaii in the US
bugs.symptoms: Calf myalgias, conjunctival suffusion; jaundice and AKI in Weil disease

bugs.name: Rickettsia rickettsii
bugs.geography: Southeastern US (NC, TN, AR, MO, VA)
bugs.symptoms: Fever, headache; rash starting on wrists/ankles spreading centripetally

bugs.name: Rickettsia prowazekii
bugs.geography: Crowding/war zones; flying squirrels in the US
bugs.symptoms: Fever, headache, centrifugal rash sparing palms/soles; Brill-Zinsser recrudescence

bugs.name: Ehrlichia chaffeensis
bugs.symptoms: Fever, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia; morulae in monocytes

bugs.name: Anaplasma phagocytophilum
bugs.symptoms: Fever, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia; morulae in neutrophils

bugs.name: Coxiella burnetii
bugs.symptoms: Atypical pneumonia and granulomatous hepatitis; culture-negative endocarditis
bugs.treatment: Doxycycline; add hydroxychloroquine for chronic endocarditis

bugs.name: Francisella tularensis
bugs.symptoms: Ulceroglandular: skin ulcer with regional lymphadenopathy; very low infectious dose

bugs.name: Brucella melitensis
bugs.symptoms: Undulant fevers, night sweats, back pain; from unpasteurized dairy

bugs.name: Cryptococcus neoformans
bugs.symptoms: Subacute headache, fever, meningismus in AIDS; India ink-positive yeast
bugs.treatment: Liposomal amphotericin B + flucytosine, then fluconazole

bugs.name: Candida albicans
bugs.symptoms: Oral thrush, esophageal/vaginal candidiasis; bloodstream infection
bugs.treatment: Echinocandin for candidemia; fluconazole for mucosal disease

bugs.name: Aspergillus fumigatus
bugs.symptoms: Halo sign on chest CT in neutropenia; positive galactomannan

bugs.name: Mucorales
bugs.symptoms: Rhino-orbital-cerebral invasion in diabetic ketoacidosis and transplant patients
bugs.treatment: Liposomal amphotericin B plus emergent surgical debridement

bugs.name: Dermatophytes (Trichophyton)
bugs.symptoms: Annular scaly tinea plaques; thickened discolored nails
bugs.treatment: Topical antifungals; oral terbinafine for onychomycosis

bugs.name: Malassezia furfur
bugs.symptoms: Greasy yellow scaly plaques on scalp, eyebrows, nasolabial folds

bugs.name: Rubella virus
bugs.symptoms: Mild fine maculopapular rash; posterior auricular lymphadenopathy

bugs.name: Measles virus
bugs.symptoms: Cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots; cephalocaudal rash
bugs.treatment: Supportive; vitamin A in severe cases; MMR for prevention

bugs.name: Human herpesvirus 6
bugs.symptoms: High fever 3-5 days then rash appears as fever defervesces

bugs.name: Varicella-zoster virus
bugs.symptoms: Dewdrop-on-rose-petal vesicles in varying stages; dermatomal rash in zoster

bugs.name: Herpes simplex virus
bugs.symptoms: Recurrent grouped vesicles on erythematous base; prodromal tingling

bugs.name: Coxsackievirus A16
bugs.symptoms: Painful oral ulcers plus vesicles on palms, soles, and buttocks

bugs.name: Molluscum contagiosum virus
bugs.symptoms: Discrete flesh-colored dome-shaped papules with central umbilication
bugs.treatment: Self-resolving; curettage or cryotherapy if treated

bugs.name: Monkeypox virus
bugs.symptoms: Centripetal rash including palms/soles; all lesions at same stage

drugs.name: Metronidazole
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug activated by parasite nitroreductase to DNA-damaging radicals
drugs.adverseEffects: Metallic taste; disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol

drugs.name: Paromomycin
drugs.disease: Luminal eradication of intestinal amebic cysts
drugs.mechanism: Aminoglycoside binding 16S rRNA on 30S ribosome; not orally absorbed
drugs.adverseEffects: GI upset only (oral); aminoglycoside toxicity if parenteral

drugs.name: Fexinidazole
drugs.disease: Early- and late-stage African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness)
drugs.mechanism: Nitroimidazole activated by nitroreductase; oral, crosses the BBB
drugs.adverseEffects: Relapse if 24-month follow-up not feasible

drugs.name: Pentamidine
drugs.disease: Early-stage Gambiense HAT in young children
drugs.mechanism: Binds parasite kinetoplast DNA; IV/IM only, poor CNS penetration
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypoglycemia then hyperglycemia; nephrotoxicity, hypotension

drugs.name: Suramin
drugs.disease: Early-stage Rhodesiense HAT in young children
drugs.mechanism: Polyanion inhibiting parasite glycolytic enzymes and NADH oxidation
drugs.adverseEffects: Immediate hypersensitivity shock; nephrotoxicity, neuropathy

drugs.name: Eflornithine
drugs.disease: Severe late-stage Gambiense HAT (part of NECT)
drugs.mechanism: Suicide inhibitor of ornithine decarboxylase, blocking polyamine synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: Bone marrow suppression; IV-only administration

drugs.name: Melarsoprol
drugs.disease: Late-stage Rhodesiense HAT with CNS involvement
drugs.mechanism: Trivalent arsenical binding parasite trypanothione and enzymes
drugs.adverseEffects: Reactive encephalopathy (sometimes fatal); coadminister prednisolone

drugs.name: Benznidazole
drugs.mechanism: Nitroreductase-activated free radical generator
drugs.adverseEffects: Photosensitive dermatitis; peripheral neuropathy; marrow suppression

drugs.name: Pentavalent antimonials
drugs.mechanism: Reduced to trivalent antimony, binding parasite sulfhydryl groups
drugs.adverseEffects: Cumulative cardiac, pancreatic, renal, and marrow toxicity

drugs.name: Miltefosine
drugs.mechanism: Disrupts parasite phospholipid metabolism; only oral antileishmanial
drugs.adverseEffects: Teratogenic; absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy

drugs.name: Pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin
drugs.mechanism: Sequential folate synthesis inhibition (DHFR + DHPS); leucovorin rescue
drugs.adverseEffects: Bone marrow suppression mitigated by leucovorin

drugs.name: Spiramycin
drugs.disease: First-trimester toxoplasmosis to prevent vertical transmission
drugs.mechanism: Macrolide that concentrates in the placenta
drugs.adverseEffects: Minimal fetal exposure; does not treat established fetal infection

drugs.name: Amphotericin B
drugs.disease: Serious systemic mycoses (cryptococcus, mucor, dimorphic fungi)
drugs.mechanism: Binds ergosterol forming membrane pores; fungicidal
drugs.adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity; 'shake and bake' infusion reactions

drugs.name: Nystatin
drugs.mechanism: Polyene binding ergosterol; topical/oral non-absorbed only
drugs.adverseEffects: Too toxic for systemic use; minimal with topical use

drugs.name: Flucytosine
drugs.mechanism: Converted by fungal cytosine deaminase to 5-FU, blocking DNA/RNA synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: Bone marrow suppression from gut conversion to 5-FU

drugs.name: Fluconazole
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits fungal 14-alpha-demethylase; best CNS penetration; no mold activity
drugs.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity; QT prolongation; CYP drug interactions

drugs.name: Voriconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole blocking ergosterol synthesis via 14-alpha-demethylase
drugs.adverseEffects: Visual disturbances / photopsia; phototoxicity raising SCC risk

drugs.name: Itraconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole inhibiting 14-alpha-demethylase; needs acidic gastric pH
drugs.adverseEffects: Negative inotrope; avoid in heart failure

drugs.name: Posaconazole
drugs.disease: Mucormycosis and prophylaxis in prolonged neutropenia
drugs.mechanism: Azole with extended spectrum covering Mucorales
drugs.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity; QT prolongation; CYP interactions

drugs.name: Ketoconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole inhibiting 14-alpha-demethylase
drugs.adverseEffects: Severe hepatotoxicity; anti-androgen effects (gynecomastia)

drugs.name: Echinocandins (caspofungin)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibit beta-1,3-glucan synthase, cracking the fungal cell wall
drugs.adverseEffects: Excellent safety; mild GI upset and flushing

drugs.name: Terbinafine
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits squalene epoxidase; ergosterol depletion plus toxic squalene buildup
drugs.adverseEffects: Taste disturbance (dysgeusia); rare severe hepatotoxicity

drugs.name: Griseofulvin
drugs.mechanism: Binds fungal microtubules disrupting mitosis; deposits in keratin
drugs.adverseEffects: CYP450 induction; disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.disease: Lyme disease, RMSF, ehrlichiosis, anaplasmosis, Q fever
drugs.mechanism: Tetracycline inhibiting bacterial 30S ribosomal protein synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: Photosensitivity; dental staining (brief courses negligible)

drugs.name: Isotretinoin
drugs.mechanism: Oral retinoid normalizing keratinization and reducing sebum
drugs.adverseEffects: Highly teratogenic; requires iPLEDGE monitoring

drugs.name: Dapsone
drugs.mechanism: Sulfone with anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial activity
drugs.adverseEffects: Hemolysis, especially in G6PD deficiency; methemoglobinemia

drugs.name: Vismodegib
drugs.disease: Locally advanced or metastatic basal cell carcinoma
drugs.mechanism: Smoothened inhibitor blocking hedgehog pathway signaling
drugs.adverseEffects: Muscle spasms, alopecia, dysgeusia; teratogenic

drugs.name: Vemurafenib
drugs.mechanism: BRAF kinase inhibitor blocking RAS/MAPK proliferation signaling
drugs.adverseEffects: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas; combine with MEK inhibitor

drugs.name: Checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1, anti-CTLA-4)
drugs.mechanism: Block T-cell checkpoints to unleash anti-tumor immune response
drugs.adverseEffects: Immune-related adverse events (colitis, dermatitis, endocrinopathies)

drugs.name: Topical 5-fluorouracil
drugs.disease: Actinic keratosis and superficial basal cell carcinoma
drugs.mechanism: Pyrimidine analog inhibiting thymidylate synthase in atypical cells
drugs.adverseEffects: Local erythema, erosion, and inflammation at treated sites

correlates.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
correlates.pathophysiology: Entamoeba trophozoites invade colon, travel via portal vein, and form necrotic liver abscesses
correlates.treatment: Metronidazole then paromomycin; drainage only if impending rupture

correlates.name: Chagas Cardiomyopathy
correlates.pathophysiology: T. cruzi persists in cardiomyocytes causing chronic immunologic dilated cardiomyopathy with apical aneurysm
correlates.treatment: Benznidazole if early; supportive heart failure/antiarrhythmic care once established

correlates.name: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: S. aureus exfoliative toxins cleave desmoglein-1 in the granular layer causing intraepidermal separation
correlates.treatment: Anti-staphylococcal IV antibiotics and supportive fluid care

correlates.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Rapid bacterial invasion of deep fascial planes with proteases, thrombosis, and tissue necrosis
correlates.treatment: Emergent surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum IV antibiotics

correlates.name: Inhalation Anthrax (Woolsorter's Disease)
correlates.pathophysiology: Inhaled spores germinate in mediastinal nodes, releasing tripartite toxin causing hemorrhagic mediastinitis
correlates.treatment: IV ciprofloxacin/doxycycline + clindamycin + additional agent; raxibacumab

correlates.name: Cryptococcal Meningitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Inhaled encapsulated yeast disseminates from lungs to CNS in HIV patients with CD4 under 100
correlates.treatment: Induction with liposomal amphotericin B + flucytosine, then fluconazole

correlates.name: Psoriasis
correlates.pathophysiology: Th17-driven keratinocyte hyperproliferation with maturation accelerated to 8-10 days
correlates.treatment: Topical steroids and vitamin D analogs, phototherapy, biologics for severe disease

correlates.name: Albinism
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal recessive tyrosinase defect; melanocytes present but cannot synthesize melanin
correlates.treatment: No cure; rigorous lifelong sun protection and dermatologic surveillance

correlates.name: Vitiligo
correlates.pathophysiology: T-cell-mediated autoimmune destruction of melanocytes producing depigmented patches
correlates.treatment: Topical corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, narrowband UVB phototherapy

correlates.name: Telogen Effluvium
correlates.pathophysiology: Stressor synchronizes anagen follicles into telogen, causing diffuse shedding ~3 months later
correlates.treatment: Address the trigger; reassurance, with full regrowth in 6-12 months

correlates.name: Acne Vulgaris
correlates.pathophysiology: Follicular hyperkeratinization, androgenic sebum overproduction, C. acnes, and inflammation
correlates.treatment: Topical retinoids and benzoyl peroxide; antibiotics; isotretinoin for severe disease

correlates.name: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Maternal rubella infection in pregnancy disrupts fetal organogenesis via cell apoptosis
correlates.treatment: Prevent with pre-pregnancy MMR; supportive care for hearing, eye, cardiac defects

correlates.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
correlates.pathophysiology: Type IV cytotoxic T-cell drug reaction causing widespread keratinocyte apoptosis and epidermal necrosis
correlates.treatment: Stop the offending drug immediately; burn-unit-level supportive care

correlates.name: Urticaria
correlates.pathophysiology: Type I IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation causing histamine-driven dermal edema
correlates.treatment: Antihistamines; identify and avoid trigger

correlates.name: Hereditary Angioedema
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal dominant C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency causing unopposed bradykinin and angioedema
correlates.treatment: C1 inhibitor concentrate, ecallantide, or icatibant (not antihistamines)

correlates.name: Atopic Dermatitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Filaggrin mutations and immune dysregulation cause barrier dysfunction and spongiotic dermatitis
correlates.treatment: Emollients, topical corticosteroids, and calcineurin inhibitors

correlates.name: Erythema Multiforme
correlates.pathophysiology: Type IV interface reaction, most often triggered by HSV, producing targetoid lesions
correlates.treatment: Treat the trigger (suppressive acyclovir for HSV); supportive care

correlates.name: Lichen Planus
correlates.pathophysiology: CD8+ T-cell attack on basal keratinocytes; associated with hepatitis C
correlates.treatment: Topical corticosteroids; self-limited over months to years

correlates.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 cause suprabasal acantholysis and flaccid bullae
correlates.treatment: Systemic corticosteroids plus rituximab or other immunosuppressants

correlates.name: Bullous Pemphigoid
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies against hemidesmosomal BP180 cause subepidermal tense bullae
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids; doxycycline plus niacinamide for milder cases

correlates.name: Dermatitis Herpetiformis
correlates.pathophysiology: IgA against tissue transglutaminase deposits at dermal papillary tips; linked to celiac disease
correlates.treatment: Strict gluten-free diet plus dapsone for rapid relief

correlates.name: Rosacea
correlates.pathophysiology: Innate immune dysregulation with elevated cathelicidin and possible Demodex mite role
correlates.treatment: Trigger avoidance, topical metronidazole/ivermectin, oral doxycycline

correlates.name: Erythema Nodosum
correlates.pathophysiology: Septal panniculitis; hypersensitivity reaction to strep, sarcoidosis, IBD, or drugs
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying cause; NSAIDs for pain

correlates.name: Seborrheic Keratosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign basaloid keratinocyte hyperplasia with horn cysts; FGFR3/PIK3CA mutations
correlates.treatment: Benign; cryotherapy or curettage if cosmetically desired

correlates.name: Acanthosis Nigricans
correlates.pathophysiology: Insulin/IGF-1 stimulation of keratinocytes; or paraneoplastic with GI adenocarcinoma
correlates.treatment: Treat insulin resistance; investigate GI cancer if sudden in older adults

correlates.name: Actinic Keratosis
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced p53 mutation causing partial-thickness keratinocyte atypia; precursor to SCC
correlates.treatment: Cryotherapy, topical 5-FU, imiquimod, photodynamic therapy

correlates.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced p53 mutations drive malignant keratinocytes invading through the basement membrane
correlates.treatment: Excision or Mohs surgery; cemiplimab for advanced disease

correlates.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced PTCH1 loss causes constitutive hedgehog pathway activation and basaloid proliferation
correlates.treatment: Surgical excision or Mohs; vismodegib for advanced disease

correlates.name: Dysplastic Nevus
correlates.pathophysiology: BRAF/NRAS mutation plus CDKN2A loss producing cytologic atypia and architectural disorder
correlates.treatment: Monitor; excise concerning lesions; surveillance if familial syndrome

correlates.name: Melanoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant melanocyte transformation from UV-induced DNA damage and BRAF V600E mutations
correlates.treatment: Wide local excision by Breslow depth; immunotherapy and BRAF/MEK inhibitors for advanced disease

correlates.name: Herpes Zoster (Shingles)
correlates.pathophysiology: Reactivation of latent VZV in a dorsal root or cranial nerve ganglion
correlates.treatment: Acyclovir/valacyclovir within 72 hours; Shingrix vaccine for prevention

correlates.name: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Herpes zoster reactivation in the geniculate ganglion involving cranial nerve VII
correlates.treatment: Acyclovir plus corticosteroids

correlates.name: Pityriasis Rosea
correlates.pathophysiology: Self-limited eruption, likely HHV-6/7, with a herald patch then Christmas-tree truncal rash
correlates.treatment: Supportive; self-resolves over 6-8 weeks
